title: IRS: Instructions for Form 941 (Rev. March 2026), Paperwork Reduction Act notice and burden estimates

history.reason: Source read directly on the access date; findings transcribed from the document.
Re-read IRS PDF page 16 for review; clarified annual units, cost definitions, bundle scope and 62-hour aggregate.

source_type: Government form instructions with burden estimates
reliability: Government document; the issuing agency is also the party imposing or administering the requirement. Publication date not shown beyond "Rev. March 2026".
findings: IRS annual burden estimates cover the Form 941 series and related employment-tax and wage-statement forms and schedules, under law as of October 1, 2025. Time includes recordkeeping, preparing/submitting forms and wage statements; out-of-pocket reporting expenses are separate, and taxes paid are excluded.

IRS says the figures are national averages that do not necessarily reflect a typical employer, and that most employers experience lower than average burden, varying considerably with the number of Forms W-2 filed.

IRS example: four Forms W-2 imply estimated annual time of 63.6 hours (15.9 x 4) and annual out-of-pocket cost of $2,480 ($620 x 4), across the reporting bundle; this is not the total monetized burden.
IRS example: 2,000 Forms W-2 imply estimated annual time of 800 hours (2,000 x 0.4) and annual out-of-pocket cost of $40,000 (2,000 x $20), across the reporting bundle.

The Annual Average Burden table lists 62 total hours and $2,760 out-of-pocket cost for filers with Form 941, and $4,890 total monetized burden. The footnote defines total monetized burden as monetized hours plus out-of-pocket costs. This aggregate differs from the per-W-2 size-band estimates.
limitations: Model-based IRS estimates, not measured time; the underlying method was not examined.
Averages across all employer types; the instructions state many employers have lower burden.
Payroll software and service providers already serve this need; their adoption and coverage were not investigated.
